paper.title: Improved Bound for Robust Causal Bandits with Linear Models

settings.name_in_paper: Robust causal bandits with linear SEMs under temporal model fluctuations (deviation budget C)
unmapped: Arms are the 2^N soft interventions on a known DAG with linear SEM X = B_a^T X + eps; reward is the leaf node X_N (non-linear in unknown weights B, B*)
Learner observes the full vector of node values X(t) after each intervention, not just the reward
Corruption is on the SEM weight matrices (model deviation D_a(t) - B_a(t)), not directly on rewards; C = max_i sum_t max_a ||[Delta_a(t)]_i||
Regret compares nominal optimal mean T*mu_{a*} with the actual (deviated) collected rewards E[X_N(t)]
Learner knows the graph structure and the mean of the exogenous noise nu
d is the maximum in-degree of the DAG and L the length of the longest causal path
Noise vector is 1-sub-Gaussian and bounded in norm by m_eps; columns of B_a have norm <= 1
settings.definition_quote: We consider a {\em linear} SEM ... $\bX=\bB^{\top} \bX+\bepsilon$ ... The noise vector $\bepsilon$ is $1$-sub-Gaussian, and its Euclidean norm is upper bounded ... $C \triangleq \max_{i\in[N]} \sum_{t=1}^T\max_{a(t)\in\mathcal{A}}\left\|\left[\Delta_{a(t)}(t)\right]_i\right\|$ ... We assume that the model deviation budgets specified by $C$ are known to the learner

symbols.m_X: upper bound on the norm of the node vector, ||X|| <= m
symbols.d_in: maximum in-degree of the causal graph (paper's d)
symbols.L: length of the longest directed causal path

conditions: kappa_min > 0 (second-moment matrices of parents have positive effective smallest eigenvalue)
tuning: beta(t,delta) = sqrt(2 log(1/delta) + d log(1 + m^2 t/(d C^2))) + 1 + m

source.label: thm:measure2
source.quote: Under a deviation budget $C$, by setting $\delta=\frac{1}{2NT}$ and confidence radius $\beta(t,\delta)$ according to Lemma~\ref{lem:beta(t)indeviation}, the average cumulative regret of \algonameRWLinSEMUCB\  is upper bounded by $\E \left[R(T)\right]\leq 2m+\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(d^{L-\frac{1}{2}}(\sqrt{T} + C)\right)$.

results.notes: Regret defined as T mu_{a*} - sum E[X_N(t)], a means-based regret, mapped to pseudo_regret. Hidden constants depend on kappa_min, kappa_max, m. Õ hides log factors including log N. The paper's 'average cumulative regret' is total expected regret. With C=1 and no deviation reduces to Õ(d^{L-1/2} sqrt T).
